comment: Frame 107, printed p. 101: the heading of the islands of the sea of Jurjān and Ṭabaristān and its four islands; then the heading of the places in which the boundaries of the countries are written, and its first countries, each with the longitude and latitude of the middle of its writing. The editor's running numbers (١٥٤٤)-(١٥٥١) and the numbers of Suhrāb [١٠٢٢]-[١٠٢٤], then [٤٩٧]-[٥٠٠]. Four lines of the editor's footnotes.

variants: L02: the words between the marks a, جزء ونصف, stand in the margin of the manuscript, written by a later hand (note a-a).
L04: a variant reading of the longitude is ڡد ن, with a line over the numerals (note b).
L05: a variant reading of the longitude is ڡح ى, with a line over the numerals (note c).

L08: a variant reading of the name is نڡه: the ن with its dot, the loop of ف or ق without dots and a final ه, joined by long strokes with small rises; the rise before the ه may also be a م: نڡمه (note d).
L09: the manuscript has اعاٮه, with a tooth without a dot before the ه; at entry (45) the name is written عانه, and at entry (1677) الغابه (note e).
L09: the editor compares the mountain معرس الأسفل (566-567) (note f).
L09: the manuscript has على for عند (note g).
L09: a variant reading of the latitude is ك ط, with a line over the numerals (note h).
L11: the editor compares the mountain لوثا (617-618), and at entry (1641) جبل اليوڡا, with the loop of ف or ق without dots (note i).
observations: The islands of the sea of al-Baṣra end on p. 100 (frame 106). L01: the heading of the next section, in larger type, centred: «* جزائر بحر جرجان وطبرستان *», the islands of the sea of Jurjān and Ṭabaristān, with a small open star with six points at each end; «جزائر» has a hamza on the tooth.

L02-L06: four islands, each with its size and the longitude and latitude of its middle, «وسطها عند طول … والعرض …», with the degrees and the minutes written with letters under one line, transcribed with {ov:…}: «جزيرة مقدار جزءين فى جزء ونصف» (L02), of two degrees by one and a half, the words «جزء ونصف» standing between two note marks a; «جزيرة مقدار جزءين فى جزء» (L03, L04), of two degrees by one; and «جزيرة مقدار جزءين فى ثلثى جزء» (L05), of two degrees by two thirds of a degree. Running numbers (١٥٤٤)-(١٥٤٧); the numbers of Suhrāb [١٠٢٢]-[١٠٢٤] stand after (١٥٤٤), (١٥٤٥) and (١٥٤٧); point 1546 has none. L06 is a short line, closed by a small open star with six points, transcribed as an asterisk, like the stars between the islands.

L07: the heading of the next section, in larger type, centred: «* المواضع الّتى تكتب فيها حدود البلدان *», the places in which the boundaries of the countries are written, with a small open star with six points at each end; «الّتى» has a shadda over the ل.

L08-L12: the countries, each with the longitude and latitude of the middle of its writing, «وسط الكتاب عند طول … والعرض …»: «بلاد نيفل الداخلة» (L08), the inner land of نيفل, at the latitude 5° 30′ beyond the equator; «غانه قوم يسمّون اغرمطين» (L09), غانه, a people called اغرمطين; «بلاد الدملى الّتى لا يكون فيها المطر» (L10), the land of الدملى, in which there is no rain; «بلاد ليبوانى الداخلة وسط كتابها» (L11), the inner land of ليبوانى, the middle of its writing; and «بلاد بمملكة البربر» (L12), the land in the kingdom of the Berbers, whose latitude follows on p. 102. Each entry ends with a small open star with six points. The running numbers run (١٥٤٨)-(١٥٥١), and the numbers of Suhrāb, after [١٠٢٤] of point 1547, are [٤٩٧]-[٥٠٠], after (١٥٤٨)-(١٥٥١), without a gap.

Signs in the text, transcribed as printed: «يسمّون» (L09) with a shadda over the م; «الّتى» (L10) with a shadda over the ل; «جزءين» with a hamza between the ز and the ي; «جزء» and «الاستواء» with a hamza; «فى», «ثلثى», «الدملى», «ليبوانى» and «الّتى» end in a ى without dots. The names «نيفل» (L08), «غانه» and «اغرمطين» (L09) and «ليبوانى» (L11) are printed with all their dots.

Numerals: «عط ل» (L02), 79° 30′; «مو {z}» (L02), 46° 0′; «مد م» (L03), 44° 40′; «ڡه ن» (L04), with the dot of the ن in the minutes, 50; «مح ل» (L04), 48° 30′; «مز ل» (L05), with the dot of the ز, 47° 30′. The loop of ف or ق without dots in the degrees of the longitude, «ڡد» (L03), «ڡه» (L04) and «ڡح» (L05), which read with ف give 84, 85 and 88, beside the longitude 79° 30′ of L02. The countries: «كو {z}» (L08, L12), 26° 0′; «ه ل» (L08), 5° 30′; «ما {z}» (L09), 41° 0′; «ك ل» (L09), 20° 30′; «مد ل» (L10), 44° 30′; «ه {z}» (L11), 5° 0′; «ك {z}» (L11), 20° 0′; «كا ل» (L12), 21° 30′.

The ح of «مح» (L04) and «ڡح» (L05) shows no dot in the bowl; the same form is a ج without its dot, 3. Transcribed as printed. The isolated ك, 20, is printed with the small inner stroke of the letter (L09, L11).

Note marks: L02, a after «فى» and a after «ونصف»; L04, b after the longitude; L05, c after the longitude; L08, d after «نيفل»; L09, e after «غانه», f after «اغرمطين», g after «عند» and h after the latitude; L11, i after «ليبوانى».
The editor's footnotes stand in four lines below a short rule at the left: notes a-i, one of them, a-a, on the text between two marks. The page number «— ١٠١ —» stands at the foot, centred.
